sourceClaims.claim: Cognitivist accounts treat ordinary moral sentences as truth-apt and their acceptance as belief-like. Noncognitivist accounts question substantial truth conditions or belief expression, although sophisticated expressivists may allow deflationary truth talk. Truth-aptness alone does not establish that any moral claim is true.
